Real harmonic node-zero uniqueness follows from a complete half-plane tiling, disk derivative identity with constant 2048/pi, weighted tile area, disk overlap <=3/(beta log alpha), and contraction <=6144e/(40000pi)<0.134. Primary Eq.(2.2) and Prop.2.3 identify the Cauchy transform and both real channels. Bergman point evaluation proves F^2 belongs to the required weighted space; vanishing real part forces zero imaginary constant, global holomorphic factorization, and real-signal injectivity. Boundary p->0 is excluded but all p>0 hold; finite supplemental tests are not substituted for quantified proof.

originality.rationale: For real L2 signals the established comparison theorem uses three real wavelets and explicitly leaves two-window sufficiency open. The new two-channel theorem proves a genuinely different implication: dense lattice zeros of the real part of a weighted Bergman square force a global sign. The source two-window frame result controls linear coefficients, not magnitudes. The inspected bandlimited theorem and 2026 eight-window complex-signal result do not cover this claim. Searches of indexed research records and primary literature found no equivalent or stronger theorem, but the historical-priority conclusion is provisional.

value.rationale: The published focal work explicitly asks whether two Poisson/Hilbert-wavelet magnitude channels could suffice without bandlimiting. The theorem replaces the three-window construction by exactly two explicit real windows for every real L2 signal, using a quantitatively new real-harmonic uniqueness mechanism. The substantial sacrifice in lattice density is acknowledged; this nevertheless resolves a genuine natural window-count existence question rather than a routine parameter variation. It does not claim optimal density, stable inversion or an algorithm.
